meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay. Who decided it?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. That's a machine's guess, and the people who sell those checkers say in writing it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student; I have their guide in my bag. What did Owen say when you asked him?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. Kids do that.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
So he got a line wrong. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare from study notes every day.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and the final draft. That's what an outline is for.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Five minutes after class with no warning, and "like, being stuck" isn't wrong. A timed piece in September proves he writes better with a weekend.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine, to put this behind him, and only that. In writing tonight, Hale: private, supervised, the rewrite mark replaces the zero, and nothing in his file. Who else has seen what you just showed me?
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday's fine. Who else has seen it?
Do we have an agreement?
When it's in my inbox tonight, we do. And I'm still waiting on who else has seen it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement in writing, and I want to know who else has seen the material you showed me. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: At her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school with the mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight and still wants to know who else has seen your evidence, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her call.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its late-night times and single large edits moved her, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own file, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with the detector score cost you, because it was a number she could not check and the vendor itself says not to rely on it alone.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing late on the night of October 28, close to the kind of night she was trying not to think about; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who else had seen the evidence, answer her plainly before moving on to Thursday's timing, so the agreement closes with nothing left open.
